subject: Predict NBA Second Half Results - Model

messages.author: 8c865e863638d71e
messages.subject: Predict NBA Second Half Results - Model
parts:
Any feedback you can give me on what may be conceptually wrong with this model, or what to try going forward would be great.  Actually, I would even be willing to pay someone money to work on this with me, so let me know if you are interested.  Thanks!

The goal of this model is to predict the second half score of an NBA game given that it's already at halftime.  The information used to predict the outcome is the Vegas full game spread which is publicly available before the game starts.  Also used is the score of the first half, the idea being that the more a team is winning the in first half the less well they will do in the second half, and vice versa.  I know for a fact that both of these are significant predictors which come close to predicting the second half outcome as best as it can be predicted without overfitting.

My hypothesis is that different teams have different tendencies in the second half in certain situations.  I suspect that these tendencies are minor, but may be enough to gain a little edge in accuracy of predictions.

So for instance, when the Cavaliers start off losing, I suspect they may be extra good (by .5 or 1 point compared to other teams on average) at making a comeback.  So to build my model, I use a hierarchical model based on teams and also three categories (3: performing extra well in the first half, 2: performing at expectation in the first half, 1: performing under expectation in the first half)

Here is my model (there are 30 teams, 3 categoryh1.  line refers to the vegas full game line, and diffh1 refers to how much the away team is winning first half)

model {
  for (i in 1:Ntotal) {
    resulth2[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i], 1 / (sigma ^ 2))
    mu[i] <- beta0[team[i], categoryh1[i]] + beta1[team[i], categoryh1[i]] * line[i] + beta2[team[i], categoryh1[i]] * diffh1[i]
  }

  for (j in 1:Nsubj) {
    for (z in 1:3) {
      beta0[j, z] ~ dnorm( beta0mu, 1)
      beta1[j, z] ~ dnorm( beta1mu, 1)
      beta2[j, z] ~ dnorm( beta2mu, 1)
    }
  }
 
  beta0mu  ~ dnorm( 0, 1)
  beta1mu  ~ dnorm( 0, 1 )
  beta2mu  ~ dnorm( 0, 1 )
  sigma ~ dnorm(1,1)
}"

I've tried this model along with changing the prior from 1 to 10, 50, 100 and none seem to be successful. 

I use 600 games to train on and 200 games to test on (and do this for a couple different seasons).  Using beta0, beta1, beta3, the teams, and categoryh1, I predict the results in the 200 games and compare them to what the Vegas line was for the second half.  Anywhere between accuracy 52%-56% is the desired result.  Below that and the model is basically like flipping a coin.  Above that and the win rate is too high to be believable.  After backtesting it is clear this model does not work it needs some improvement!

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Predict NBA Second Half Results - Model
parts:
Hi Daniel,

A couple of points:
1. Switch over to Stan and you'll get a little more response. This model should be easy to change to Stan.
2. Substantively, why do you think you should use the Vegas line as a predictor? That seems like a bad idea.... but maybe the Vegas market is big enough where they are actually predicting outcomes. (I don't believe it, but could be convinced the Vegas lines are now accurate.)



Daniel

messages.author: 8c865e863638d71e
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Predict NBA Second Half Results - Model
parts:
1) Okay I started changing it to Stan, I'll respond when I can get that done
2) Note I am using the full game line to predict the second half outcome.  So if Vegas has a line where a team is expected to win the game by 20 points, it is ROUGHLY accurate to expect a second half win by 10.  The Vegas line can be trusted since people can bet $20,000+ on a game in a single bet.  In contrast, the second half line has a limit of $5,000.  The market for the full game line is big and efficient.  The market for the second half is relatively speaking less efficient than the full game line.  I can expand on this if you still doubt...
